raw_response:
I've been farming this small plot in Quzhou for thirty years, and I know every corner of it. My 1.1 mu isn't much, but it feeds into my family's security, and I treat it with care. My husband and children work off-farm in the city, sending money home, which means I manage the fields mostly by myself. Labor is tight, so I can't afford wasteful practices. With well irrigation available, I have reliable water, but electricity for the pump costs money, so I irrigate only when the crops truly need it.

Right now, it's early spring, and the winter wheat I planted last October is greening up. I already gave it the overwinter water last winter. This week, I will apply the spring top-dressing—urea—when I irrigate for the jointing stage. I will irrigate once more at grain filling if the weather stays dry. For weeds and the occasional powdery mildew or rust, I will spray twice: once soon for broadleaf weeds, and again later if disease shows up. I use an improved wheat variety that the local supply store recommends; it performs well here and I save some seed, but I refresh it every few years. I expect about 500 jin per mu, maybe a bit more if the season is kind.

After the wheat comes off in early June, I have very little time before summer maize must go in. I will hire a combine to harvest the wheat, then immediately plant hybrid maize seed directly into the stubble without ploughing—no-tillage saves me three to four precious days and keeps soil moisture. Hybrid seed is non-negotiable for maize; the yield difference is too large. I will fertilize at planting and side-dress nitrogen at the big-flush stage. I'll irrigate two or three times: at planting if it's dry, at jointing, and definitely at tasseling because silk drying is the enemy of good ears. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide once for corn borer. If all goes well, I should get around 550 jin per mu of maize.

My phosphorus and potassium come from compound fertilizer applied at sowing for both crops, while nitrogen is split between basal and top-dressing. I keep inputs moderate because my plot is small and I know from experience that throwing more fertilizer at it doesn't always pay back on this land.
